node.summary: A workspace participating in the mesh — a repo checkout or an isolated git worktree.
details: Base node vs worktree clone node — a clone isolates parallel work without conflicts.
Shows health (online/offline) alongside git state (branch · ahead/behind · dirty).
Multiple nodes can share the same daemon.

p2p.summary: How the selected coordinator reaches each remote node over WebRTC.
details: direct — a direct host/STUN path; lowest latency.
relay — TURN-relayed; works through restrictive networks but is slower.
disconnected / failed — no live P2P link from the coordinator right now.
P2P connectivity is shown as transport and RTT chips on each node card (and in the node detail panel), not as a graph edge.

session.summary: An agent CLI session running on a node.
details: status = idle / generating / waiting_approval.
Distinguishes coordinator sessions (which dispatch and collect work) from delegated worker sessions (which do the work).

task.summary: A single unit of work handled by the queue-based pull model.
details: States: pending → assigned → completed / failed / cancelled.
Idle nodes claim from the queue automatically; direct dispatch targets a specific session.

mission.summary: A multi-task batch aimed at one goal, and the durable record of that effort.
details: States: active / paused / completed / abandoned.
Progress is derived from the states of its member tasks.

refinery.summary: The process of safely converging and merging a worktree branch into the base.
details: Config-driven (.adhdev/refine.*) — guarded by a patch-equivalence preflight and a no-op guard.
ff-only by principle; no force-push.
If a submodule commit is unreachable from origin it must be published → classified as blocked_review.

completion.summary: Completion of delegated work is persisted to the queue (pending-events).
details: The coordinator learns of completion via periodic polling or events.
Because it is persisted to the queue, completion signals are never lost.

convergence.summary: After worktree work, each branch is classified into exactly one final state.
details: merged_to_main — merged into the base.
pushed_feature_branch_needs_merge — pushed, awaiting merge.
blocked_review — held back by review/reachability issues.
cleanup_candidate — ready to clean up.
not_mergeable — cannot be merged.

blueprint.summary: The plan view: live queue work and its task dependencies on one canvas.
details: One axis — dependency depth, left to right. Root tasks are ordered newest first.
Cards carry their own time, so position never has to encode it.
Finished dependency chains fold away so live work stays in view.

routingPreview.summary: A read-only forecast of where a hypothetical task would land.
details: Shown per difficulty; a task pinned to a node gets its own pinned preview (📌).
It is a prediction, not the owner — a card that already ran shows its real node below.

worktree.summary: A node backed by a git worktree rather than the main checkout.
details: Labelled by its branch (⎇). Lets several tasks run on one machine without sharing a branch.
Orphan worktrees are reported as cleanup candidates and are never deleted automatically.

about.heroTitle: Control your local CLI agents from anywhere — web or mobile.
about.heroDesc: ADHDev Cloud surfaces the agents running on your machines in your browser: send prompts, approve actions, orchestrate work across machines, and get notified on your phone — code flows P2P directly to your daemon, never through the server.

mesh.sectionTitle: Parallel agents that don't step on each other.
mesh.sectionSubtitle: Running agents in parallel is the easy part — every tool does it now. The hard part is what comes after: a pile of branches that still have to be checked and merged. ADHDev does that for you, so finished work arrives on main instead of in your review queue.
mesh.refineryTitle: Finished work merges to main on its own
mesh.refineryDesc: Anyone can run ten agents at once. ADHDev then checks each branch against your project's own tests and lint, merges the ones that pass cleanly into main, and tidies up — automatically, and never with a force-push. Anything unclear is held back for you to review instead of merged.
mesh.asyncTitle: You talk to one place. It runs the rest.
mesh.asyncDesc: You hand work to a single coordinator, and it runs every agent across every machine for you. It only pings you when something needs approval or finishes — so there's no queue of agent windows to watch and nothing to sit in front of.
mesh.crossPlatformTitle: Mac, Windows, Linux — all at once
mesh.crossPlatformDesc: Send a task to a specific operating system with one tag. A single prompt can build, test, or verify across Mac, Windows, and Linux machines you already own — in parallel, with no SSH setup and no virtual machines.
mesh.monoDesc: Real production repos nest submodules — exactly where naive auto-merge breaks. ADHDev handles them safely: it makes sure submodule changes are published and pointed at correctly before it touches main. This project is itself a repo with two submodules, merged this way every day.
mesh.crossDesc: Have the coordinator ask the same read-only question to several machines and models at once, then compare where they agree and disagree — more trustworthy than one agent's answer.
mesh.availableOn: Connect a machine and open the Repo Mesh page to get started.

compare.sectionTitle: Everyone runs agents in parallel. Not everyone keeps them out of each other's way.
compare.sectionSubtitle: Local CLIs spawn subagents; desktop orchestrators fan work across worktrees with a native UI. Both stop at the branch — reviewing and merging is left to you. Here's how they compare, including where each of them is the better fit.
compare.rowLandsMainLocalCli: You run the gates and merge by hand
compare.rowLandsMainDesktop: Parallelizes the work, then hands you the branches to review
compare.rowLandsMainAdhdev: The Refinery runs your repo's gates, checks patch equivalence, and rebases + merges onto main only if it hasn't moved — unattended, no force-push
compare.rowSubmodulesLocalCli: No merge automation to be aware of them
compare.rowSubmodulesDesktop: Worktree parallelism, but the merge is yours to get right
compare.rowSubmodulesAdhdev: Submodule-aware convergence: reachability gate, patch-equivalence check, atomic pointer bump — dogfooded on this monorepo daily
compare.rowAsyncLocalCli: One session at a time, synchronously
compare.rowAsyncDesktop: You supervise each agent window yourself
compare.rowAsyncAdhdev: One coordinator drives every worker on an event loop — it waits on completion/approval events, you don't poll or babysit
compare.rowMultiMachineDesktop: Bound to the one machine it runs on
compare.rowMultiMachineAdhdev: Remote daemons over P2P — Mac, Windows, and Linux nodes in one mesh, no SSH plumbing
compare.rowParallelBranchLocalCli: Subagents share one working tree — concurrent writes collide
compare.rowParallelBranchDesktop: One git worktree per task — a core strength
compare.rowParallelBranchAdhdev: One git worktree per node — parallel across machines, not just cores
compare.rowBrowser: Drive it from a browser or phone
compare.rowBrowserLocalCli: You have to be at the terminal
compare.rowBrowserDesktop: Native desktop app — you're at that desk
compare.rowBrowserAdhdev: Web-first: control sessions and approve from any browser or phone
compare.rowNativeAppDesktop: Polished native window — genuinely nicer to sit in front of
compare.rowNativeAppAdhdev: We're web-first — a browser tab, not a native app
compare.rowRestartsLocalCli: State lives in a session — close it and it's gone
compare.rowRestartsDesktop: State tied to the app process
compare.rowRestartsAdhdev: Missions persist to disk and resume after a coordinator or daemon restart — append-only audit trail
compare.rowCrossCheckLocalCli: One agent's take, no second opinion
compare.rowCrossCheckAdhdev: The coordinator sends the same read-only question to agents on different machines and providers and compares where they diverge
compare.footnote: For a single machine, a single branch, a one-shot task — a local CLI with subagents is lighter and works great, and a native desktop orchestrator is a nicer place to sit. Repo Mesh earns its keep when work fans out across machines and branches, needs to survive restarts, and should land on main automatically — controlled from wherever you are.

what.sectionSubtitle: Vendor-neutral by design. Run Claude Code on the Mac, Codex on the Windows GPU box, Cursor CLI for review passes — all in the same mesh, driven from the same dashboard. Switch vendors without switching platforms.
what.cliTitle: Drive any terminal agent from the web
what.cliDesc: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor CLI, Antigravity CLI, Grok, Kimi, and OpenCode — launched on your machine through a PTY adapter with proper resume and reconnect, driven from your browser. Send prompts and provide visual context instantly (paste, drag & drop, or upload multiple images at once).
what.uiDesc: Cloud-hosted at adhf.dev — drive every agent from a laptop or phone, whether you're at your desk or away from it.
what.ideDesc: Cursor, VS Code, VSCodium, Windsurf, Antigravity, Kiro, PearAI, Trae. Read live chat, send prompts, switch sessions, capture screenshots.
what.p2pDesc: Chat, commands, and screenshots flow directly between your browser and your daemon over WebRTC — your code never routes through the server. The cloud handles sign-in, connection setup and session status. The one exception: approval push notifications include up to 80 characters of what you're approving.

quotaPolicy.title: Quota-aware routing
quotaPolicy.description: When a node reports how much of its AI provider quota is left, the coordinator can skip nodes that are nearly exhausted and prefer nodes with more headroom. These thresholds decide when that happens. Missing or outdated readings are always ignored, so a node is never excluded on stale data.
quotaPolicy.sessionMinHint: Skip a provider whose short rolling window has less than this left.
quotaPolicy.weeklyMinHint: Skip a provider whose weekly window has less than this left.
quotaPolicy.resetImminentHint: Ignore a low session window when it resets within this long.
quotaPolicy.staleAfterHint: Fallback only: a measured window stays valid until its own reset; this age limit applies just to readings without a reset time.
quotaPolicy.spreadBonusHint: How strongly more remaining quota is preferred. Never overrides a task-difficulty match.
quotaPolicy.sessionAxisWeeklyHeadroomHint: Only prioritize an imminent 5-hour session-window reset when weekly quota remaining is at or above this. Unused 5-hour quota is lost forever, but burning it when the weekly window is already tight costs more than it saves.
quotaPolicy.blankMeansDefault: Leave a field blank to use its default (shown as the greyed-out value).
